items.title: Ed Soph interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 9, 2024
items.q: The interviewee only responds with 'Mm-hmm' and 'Yeah' to the interviewer's introduction of Neal Caine and a quote attributed to him. No personal interaction or direct relationship is described.

ctx.x: singer was all pissed off because Buddy wasn’t reading the chart and evidently wasn’t playing things that the guy wanted, was supposed to play. So Dorsey turned to the singer and said, “Don’t worry, it’ll be fine tonight.” So Ray came back for the show that night and he said that Buddy played things that even he didn’t hear could be played. And you know Rich’s aural (A-U-R) memory is the equivalent of a photographic memory. He could hear something once — Joe LaBarbera, who used to rehearse new charts for the band…

Along those same lines, I’m going to read a quote here from a bass player named Neal Caine, who is a fairly young man, I think he’s from New Orleans, a marvelous player who played here. And he was addressing the issue — I think I asked him about bass solos.
